question: Which XGI session requests does the session-mode-2 path of the version 1.3 image issue for browse, search by identifier, join, details, and teardown, and which request fields, result-buffer fields, QoS fields, and advertised session data does the guest read or produce?

scope.modeTwoTable: Session table 0x82160450 installed by factory 0x82CA28F0 for modes other than 1, and its methods between 0x82C9C5F8 and 0x82C9D678.
scope.sessionWrapper: XSession wrapper class with vtable 0x82160630 and methods between 0x82C99018 and 0x82C9C5F8, used by both session modes.
scope.requestWrappers: Guest XGI and XLiveBase request wrappers between 0x82A1E770 and 0x82A1FAD8 that call XMsgStartIORequest 0x82E926F4 or XMsgInProcessCall 0x82E92714.
scope.boundary: Static request shapes, buffer reads and writes, and completion handling. Runtime delivery, the visible UI that selects mode 2, gameplay transport after a mode-2 join, ranked arbitration and statistics, and the runtime values of game-setup globals remain outside this record.

dependencies.use: Supplies the mode split between tables 0x82160348 and 0x82160450, the mode-2 manager entries, and the first identification of the 0x000B0016 and 0x000B001B producers.
Supplies the earlier closure of state function 0x82C9D338, QoS producer 0x82C99628, and request-buffer producer 0x82C9CF70, which this record places inside the mode-2 table.
Supplies the create wrapper 0x82A1EB38 exit groups and the destructor chain to delete request 0x000B0011 that this record reuses for teardown.

modeTwoTable.slots: Table 0x82160450: +0x00 0x822E5360, +0x0C 0x82C9D338 (state step), +0x10 0x82C9CC68 (release), +0x2C 0x82C9C980 (host), +0x30 0x82C9D080 (browse), +0x34 0x82C9CF70 (search by identifier), +0x38 0x82C9C968 (cancel), +0x3C 0x821B1690 (returns 1), +0x5C 0x82C9C950 (result count), +0x60 0x82C9C928 (index check), +0x64 0x82C9D288 (host name), +0x6C 0x82C9C8E0 (QoS round-trip time), +0x70 0x82C9C8A0, +0x74 0x82C9C828, +0x78 0x82C9C7E8, +0x7C 0x82C9C9F8, +0x80 0x82C9CBC0, +0x8C 0x82C9CC10, +0xA0 0x82C9D560, +0xF8 0x82C9C6A8 (record pointer), and +0xFC 0x82C9C680 (returns 60).
modeTwoTable.comparison: Table 0x82160348 holds 0x82C9F320 (QR2 host), 0x82C9DA48 (LAN browse), 0x822DF8A0 (returns 0), and 0x82C9D978 at +0x2C, +0x30, +0x34, and +0x3C.
modeTwoTable.host: Mode-2 host slot 0x82C9C980 only dispatches slot +0x38 and returns 1. Slot +0x38 target 0x82C9C968 calls XMsgCancelIORequest 0x82E92B24 on the request at +0x28 when state +0x1C is 1. Session creation for a host therefore runs through the shared XSession wrapper, not this table.
modeTwoTable.objectFields: The 128-byte object built by 0x82C9CD68 keeps the user index at +0x44, a byte at +0x48 that selects the search-by-identifier path, the request state at +0x1C, the result-buffer size at +0x20, the result buffer at +0x24, an XOVERLAPPED at +0x28 whose first word is polled for 997, the context count at +0x4C, the context array at +0x50, and the QoS lookup object at +0x7C. Reset helper 0x82C9CB18 first calls listener slot +0x1C with event 1 and its own slot +0x10, then clears these fields and sets +0x44 to -1.

browse.gate: 0x82C9D080 requires network-readiness gate 0x82E476B0, then 0x82CB1140(user, 1), which returns true only when XamUserGetSigninState 0x82E92A74 reports 2. On a sign-in failure it calls XamShowSigninUI 0x82E929A4 with (1, 2) and returns 2.
browse.sizeProbe: 0x82C9C5F8 calls 0x82A1F310(0, user, 200, 0, 0, null, null, &object+0x20) with null results and null overlapped; it accepts return 122 with a nonzero size.
browse.contexts: 0x82C9CE10 copies a caller vector of pointers at +0x14 through +0x18, each to a 12-byte {id, value, string} record built by 0x82E47C20, into an 8-byte-per-entry array at +0x50 and stores the entry count at +0x4C.
browse.request: 0x82C9D080 calls 0x82A1F310 at 0x82C9D16C with procedure index 0, the user index, 200 results, zero properties, a 16-bit context count equal to the stored count minus one, a null property pointer, the context array, &object+0x20, the buffer at +0x24, and the XOVERLAPPED at +0x28. It sets state +0x1C to 1 on return 0 or 997.
browse.wrapper: 0x82A1F310 requires the size word to be at least 8 + 1326 * results; otherwise, or when the buffer pointer is null, it writes that requirement and returns 122. It zeroes the first two buffer words and submits XMsgStartIORequest app 0xFB message 0x000B0016 with a 32-byte request: +0x00 procedure index, +0x04 user index, +0x08 result count, +0x0C 16-bit property count, +0x0E 16-bit context count, +0x10 property pointer, +0x14 context pointer, +0x18 buffer size, +0x1C buffer pointer. With an overlapped it returns 997; status 0x80155207 returns 122 with the size written, and any other negative status returns 1627.
browse.stateStep: 0x82C9D338 waits until the XOVERLAPPED first word is not 997, allocates the 2448-byte QoS lookup object with vtable 0x82160700 and the result buffer at +0x04, calls 0x82C99628, and sets state 2. When the lookup result at +0x98C is null or its second word is zero it sets state 3, then calls the listener at +0x14 through slot +0x1C with event 2 and the index for every result, followed by event 5.

searchById.source: 0x82C9CF70 sets +0x48 to 1 and applies the same 0x82CB1140(user, 1) check, but on failure returns 0 without the sign-in UI; it then calls 0x82A1E8D0(user, stack buffer). That wrapper issues XMsgInProcessCall app 0xFC message 0x00058023, which the maintained SDK labels XMessageGameInviteGetAcceptedInfo and fails.
searchById.identifier: The 64-bit identifier passed to the search is loaded from offset 0x14 of the 0x00058023 output buffer.
searchById.request: 0x82A1F3F0 requires at least 1334 bytes, zeroes the first two buffer words, and submits XMsgStartIORequest app 0xFB message 0x000B001B with a 20-byte request: +0x00 user index, +0x04 64-bit identifier, +0x0C buffer size, +0x10 buffer pointer. 0x82C9CF70 probes the size, allocates the returned size at +0x24, and submits with the XOVERLAPPED at +0x28.
searchById.completion: When state 3 is reached on this path, a result count of exactly 1 first calls self slot +0x40 and then listener slot +0x0C with 3 and 0; any other count calls listener slot +0x0C with 3 and 9.
searchById.qualification: The guest reaches this path only after the 0x00058023 request succeeds. Browse-list joins use the stored search records and do not issue 0x000B001B.

resultLayout.header: Buffer word +0x00 is the record count and word +0x04 is the record-array pointer; 0x82C9C6A8 returns pointer + index * 0x5C.
resultLayout.record: Record offsets read by the guest: +0x00 eight-byte session identifier, +0x08 36-byte host address, +0x2C 16-byte key, +0x3C, +0x40, +0x44, and +0x48 slot counts, +0x4C property count, +0x50 context count, +0x54 property-array pointer, +0x58 context-array pointer. 0x82C9C680 reports 60 bytes as the session-information size.
resultLayout.slotReaders: 0x82C9C8A0 returns +0x48 plus +0x44. 0x82C9C7E8 returns +0x48 plus +0x40. 0x82C9C828 returns slot +0x70 plus +0x40 plus +0x3C.
resultLayout.properties: Property entries are 24 bytes with the identifier at +0x00. 0x82C9C760 returns the 32-bit word at entry +0x10 for property 0x1000003B. 0x82C9C6D8 returns the 64-bit value at entry +0x10 of property 0x20000039. 0x82C9D1B8 skips property 0x20000039 and converts the pointer at entry +0x14 of property 0x40008109 into a title string for host-name slot +0x64.
resultLayout.contexts: Context entries are 8 bytes, identifier then value. Without the +0x48 path, 0x82C9CA08 searches the record's context array for the requested identifier.
resultLayout.interpretation: These offsets agree with the public Xbox 360 XSESSION_SEARCHRESULT shape: XSESSION_INFO of 60 bytes, open public, open private, filled public, and filled private slots, then property and context counts and pointers, with XUSER_PROPERTY and XUSER_CONTEXT entries. Property 0x40008109 has the public X_PROPERTY_GAMER_HOSTNAME value.

qosLookup.call: 0x82C99628 is the only direct caller of the NetDll_XNetQosLookup wrapper 0x827F10F0 (call at 0x82C996F4). For each record it stores pointers to record +0x08, +0x00, and +0x2C in three 200-entry arrays at lookup +0x0C, +0x32C, and +0x64C, then requests all records with 8 probes, no bits-per-second limit, no flags, no event, and output at +0x98C.
qosLookup.readers: 0x82C9C8E0 returns the 16-bit word at +0x16 of entry index * 24 in the lookup result, or 2500 when no lookup object exists. 0x82C997F0 and 0x82C99790 treat entry +0x0E as a byte count and entry +0x10 as a pointer to 12-byte records, returning record word 0 and word 1.
qosLookup.use: On the +0x48 path, 0x82C9CA08 reads context values from those 12-byte QoS records instead of the search record. Slot +0x80 target 0x82C9CBC0 returns context 55 from the QoS records on that path and property 0x1000003B from the search record otherwise.
qosLookup.interpretation: Under the public XNQOS layout the reads are the per-host median round-trip time, data length, and data pointer. The guest waits for the second header word, the pending count, to reach zero before completing the list.

hostAdvertisement.contexts: Game-setup builder 0x82D8CDA8 fills the settings object passed to the XSession wrapper from the game-setup object whose pointer is stored at global 0x8314EFC8. It sets context 0x800A to 0 when that object's word +0x04 equals 5 and to 1 otherwise, context 0x800B to 0, 1, 2, or 3 from word +0x118, contexts 7, 4, 5, and 11 from words +0xFC through +0x108 when nonnegative, and context 55 from global 0x8312B8D4.
hostAdvertisement.settingsBytes: The same builder sets byte +0x04 when word +0x04 is 5, byte +0x05 when it is 2, 4, or 5, byte +0x06 and byte +0x07 from game-object queries, and stores public and private slot counts at +0x08 and +0x0C.
hostAdvertisement.properties: 0x82D8F398 sets property 0x2000003A to zero and property 0x1000003B to the 32-bit value of global 0x8312B8D4 through XGIUserSetPropertyEx wrapper 0x8280E230. Host create method 0x82C9B668 sets property 0x20000039 to the user's XUID from XamUserGetXUID.
hostAdvertisement.setters: 0x8280E110 issues message 0x000B0006 with a 24-byte request and 0x8280E1A0 issues 0x000B0007 with a 32-byte request. Both create methods issue 0x000B0006 once for each settings context.
hostAdvertisement.qosListen: 0x82C99120 copies the settings contexts into 12-byte records of id, value, and a guest pointer. 0x82C99018 calls NetDll_XNetQosListen through 0x827F10D0 with the session identifier at session +0x0C, those records, their byte length, zero bits per second, and flags 5. 0x82C9C360 invokes them after a successful create only when registry slot +0x130 returns nonzero; migrate method 0x82C9BF98 also calls both at 0x82C9C0D8 and 0x82C9C0E8.
hostAdvertisement.qualification: Global 0x8312B8D4 is zero in the static image and has one modeled reader; its runtime writer is not established. The 72-byte QoS payload of an earlier System Link capture corresponds to six such records; which conditional context was absent is not established.

sessionLifecycle.table: Vtable 0x82160630: +0x00 0x822E5520 (destructor), +0x04 0x82C9B668 (host create), +0x08 0x82C9B4B8 (join create), +0x0C 0x82C9C278 (message 0x000B0018), +0x10 0x82C9B408 (0x000B0014), +0x14 0x82C9C468 (0x000B0015, 0x000B001D, 0x000B0018), +0x1C 0x82C9B2E0 (0x000B001D), +0x20 0x82C9B0D0 (0x000B0012), +0x24 0x82C9AF78 (0x000B0013), +0x28 0x82C9BF98 and +0x2C 0x82C9AE68 (0x000B001E), +0x58 0x82C9ADC8 (0x000B001D), +0x74 0x82C9C360 (create and QoS listen), +0x78 0x82C99368, +0x80 0x82C9B918 (create flags). Constructor 0x82C9BC38 stores the vtable and sets handle +0x4C to -1.
sessionLifecycle.createFlags: 0x82C9B918 returns 0x2E, or 0x43E when settings context 0x800A is 0, when registry slot +0x94 returns true and settings byte +0x05 is set; 0x20 when that slot returns true and the byte is clear; 0x706 when the slot returns false and the byte is set; otherwise 0. When the slot returns true and settings byte +0x07 is clear it adds 0x100. Host create ORs in 1.
sessionLifecycle.create: 0x82C9B820 proceeds only while handle +0x4C is -1 and, when registry slot +0x94 returns true, only when its second argument is 1000; it then calls create wrapper 0x82A1EB38 with flags +0x50, user +0x48, public and private slot counts, nonce +0x58, session information +0x0C, a waited overlapped, and handle +0x4C. Join create 0x82C9B4B8 first copies a 60-byte session information argument to +0x0C and rejects any other length.
sessionLifecycle.join: 0x82C9B0D0 compares the first 36 bytes of a member record with the local member at +0x04. A match issues 0x000B0012 through 0x82A1EE50 with the count and user indices (+0x24, +0x48) from the local record and private-slot bytes from the argument record +0x58; otherwise 0x82A1EEF8 sends the XUIDs at +0x28. Leave 0x82C9AF78 uses the same comparison for 0x000B0013 through 0x82A1EFA0 or 0x82A1F048.
sessionLifecycle.details: 0x82C9B2E0 and 0x82C9ADC8 call 0x82A1F908 (message 0x000B001D, 24-byte request) with a 128-byte output. 0x82C9B2E0 returns true when output +0x0C lacks bit 0x08, and otherwise only when output +0x18 is at least the number of members needing a public slot. 0x82C9ADC8 returns false only when output +0x0C has bit 0x100.
sessionLifecycle.teardown: Destructor chain 0x822E5520, 0x82C9BB38, 0x82C9ACC0 issues 0x000B0011 through 0x82A1EDA0 when handle +0x4C is not 0 or -1, closes the handle, and writes -1. Mode-2 table release 0x82C9CC68 cancels a pending search, frees the context array at +0x50 and the result buffer at +0x24, and destroys the QoS lookup object at +0x7C.
sessionLifecycle.shared: Every direct caller of the 0x000B0010 through 0x000B0015, 0x000B0018, 0x000B001A, 0x000B001D, and 0x000B001E wrappers lies between 0x82C9ACC0 and 0x82C9C5F8; 0x000B0025 is issued from 0x82CA8750. Table 0x82160450 issues only XGI messages 0x000B0016 and 0x000B001B, plus XLiveBase message 0x00058023 at 0x82C9CFC4.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra queries against a disposable copy of the version 1.3 project repaired for the 0x827F7C50 thunk block (40 slots patched, 15 noreturn flags cleared, zero rebuild errors), exact-function generated-code reads where Ghidra cannot decode inline 64-bit stores, and comparison with the maintained SDK XGI and XLiveBase handlers.

entries.result: Browse, search by identifier, and the state step that drives QoS lookup and listener events.
Message 0x00058023 supplies the identifier for message 0x000B001B, 20-byte request, 1334-byte minimum.
92-byte records with slot counts, 24-byte properties, and 8-byte contexts.
One lookup caller; round-trip time and 12-byte context records; host listen with the same records.
Shared create, join, leave, details, and delete with mode-dependent create flags.

currentEvidence.qualification: Generated windows supply instruction text where the 32-bit decoder truncates; they corroborate the static control flow but are not runtime proof. XGI message names and structure field names are public-SDK and maintained-SDK interpretation; the guest facts are the offsets, sizes, and constants recorded here.

catalogPromotion.result: Catalog delta is zero. Tables 0x82160450 and 0x82160630 are candidates for vtable catalog entries when an implementation consumes them.

guards: Do not infer that ReRevved or any emulator has run session mode 2; no runtime observation of this path is recorded.

Do not assume mode-2 gameplay uses GT2 on VDP port 1000; GT2 connect method 0x82CA0258 has no direct caller and three table references, and the transport object chosen after a mode-2 join is not established.
Do not treat the context count passed to 0x000B0016 as the full array; the guest passes the stored count minus one.
Do not write result properties or contexts outside the caller buffer on the strength of this record; the guest frees only its buffer, and ownership of any other allocation is not established.
Do not identify the game-setup values that select create flags 0x2E, 0x20, 0x43E, or 0x706 with visible menu entries.
Do not record the runtime value of global 0x8312B8D4 from the static zero.
Do not equate registry slot +0x94 with session mode or with Xbox LIVE versus System Link; the record ties create flags only to that slot and settings byte +0x05.
conclusion: Session mode 2 browses by calling XGI message 0x000B0016 with procedure 0, 200 results, the settings contexts, and a buffer of 8 + 1326 bytes per result, after requiring sign-in state 2 (signed in to Live). It reads 92-byte records for session identifier, host address, key, four slot counts, 24-byte properties (0x1000003B, 0x20000039, 0x40008109), and 8-byte contexts, then runs one QoS lookup over every record and completes the list when no probe is pending, using median round-trip time. Search by identifier (0x000B001B, 20-byte request, 1334-byte buffer) serves only the accepted-invite path through XLiveBase message 0x00058023, and on that path reads contexts from 12-byte records in the host QoS data. Create, join, leave, details, start, end, modify, migrate, and delete are shared with System Link in the XSession wrapper class at vtable 0x82160630; its create flags are selected by settings byte +0x05 and registry slot +0x94: 0x2E, 0x43E when context 0x800A is 0, 0x20, or 0x706, plus 0x100 when invites are off and 1 for a host. Which session mode reaches which branch is not tied statically to slot +0x94. Both creates publish up to seven contexts, host create also sets the XUID property 0x20000039, and a QoS listen payload carries of the same context records; 0x82D8F398 also sets properties 0x2000003A and 0x1000003B, on a path not attributed to host or client.
